title: Pioneer transcription factors direct tissue-specific cohesin chromatin entry and three-dimensional genome organization.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed all files in GEO series GSE293172 (ChIP-seq, 68 samples), GSE293073 (Hi-C, 7 .hic files, 119 MB-1.7 GB), GSE293071 (RNA-seq count CSVs). Downloaded and parsed all 16 peak files (narrowPeak/BED): 22Rv1 prostate-cancer NIPBL 26,575 peaks (0h) and 26,551 (24h after FOXA1 degradation); A549 lung NIPBL 11,343 (control), 2,576 (FOXA1 knockdown), 3,110 (ETS1 knockdown); FOXA1 wild-type/R219S NIPBL 18,533/1,349; RAD21 14,384-41,263; H3K27ac 36,666-41,698. Overlaps computed: only 19% of 22Rv1 NIPBL peaks overlap A549 NIPBL peaks; 65% of 0h peaks persist at 24h. 0 duplicate intervals; median width 516 bp. GEO metadata states hg19 (human) and mm10 (mouse).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Only the abstract was available (no open full text, no PMCID). Paper's own peak counts, replicate strategy, and motif results were not checked. Mouse liver/lung/stomach NIPBL and LNCaP NIPBL exist only as bigWig signal tracks (263-505 MB each, over the 50 MB cap), not opened.

a1_downloadable.note: Public GEO series, no login; peak files 32 KB-1 MB downloaded directly. Checked in files.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Binary 'NIPBL bound here' label comes straight from narrowPeak intervals; only genome binning and sampling of unbound background windows are needed (standard, ~hours). A 'FOXA1-dependent site' label would have to be constructed by overlapping conditions, so that variant is weaker. Checked in files.

a3_inputs_present.note: Input is DNA sequence at hg19 coordinates; needs one reference-genome download, not thousands of lookups. Checked coordinates in files.

a4_units_stated.note: Standard MACS2 (a peak-calling tool) narrowPeak columns: fold enrichment, -log10 p and q values; genome build hg19 stated in GEO metadata. Checked.

a5_enough_rows.note: 26,575 NIPBL peaks in 22Rv1 and 11,343 in A549 as positives, plus as many background windows as wanted. Counted in files.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: <1 GB (peak files ~5 MB total plus hg19 reference ~0.9 GB gzipped)
a6_fits_laptop.note: Baseline motif/k-mer model or cached DNA language-model embeddings runs on CPU. Hi-C and bigWig files are not needed for the core task.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: GEO sample count (68 ChIP-seq samples) matches the series summary; paper's peak counts could not be compared because no full text is available.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels are peak calls from measured ChIP-seq (chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing) reads by a statistical threshold, not another model's prediction and not computed from DNA sequence.

B1.why: One peak file per condition; joins are by genomic interval overlap, not a key. Seen in files.

B2.why: Parses cleanly, but chromosome naming mixed ('1' in dTAG files vs 'chr1' elsewhere). Seen in files.

B3.why: Same lab and pipeline, but peak counts swing with depth (1,349 vs 18,533 for R219S vs WT).

B4.why: No censored values; binary peak membership with continuous fold enrichment.

B5.why: 0 duplicate intervals in the 22Rv1 NIPBL file. Checked.

B6.why: narrowPeak is a standard format and GEO states hg19; no methods text available beyond GEO.

C1.why: Cross-cell-line transfer (22Rv1 to A549) is informative either way; within-line accuracy alone is not.

C2.why: No NIPBL-specific model found, but sequence-to-binding and sequence-to-3D-genome models are numerous.

C3.why: Unique application: cohesin-loader binding never modelled, but the task type is standard.

C4.why: NIPBL ChIP-seq is lab-based, costly, and must be repeated per cell type or tissue.

C5.why: Obvious dummy baselines (GC content, FOXA1/ETS motif scan); no published ML number.

D1.why: DNABERT-2 and Nucleotide Transformer, open-weight DNA language models, fit 500-bp windows.

D2.why: ~50k windows of 1 kb can be embedded once on CPU, then a linear head trained.

D3.why: DNABERT-2 permissively licensed; AlphaGenome alternative is non-commercial.

E1.why: Hold out whole chromosomes; 24 chromosomes present in 22Rv1 file.

E2.why: 24 chromosomes give many held-out groups of reasonable size.

E3.why: GC-content and motif-count logistic regression are easy dummies.

E4.why: NIPBL tracks are single replicates; only H3K27ac has two replicates per condition.

E5.why: RAD21 peaks should be predictable from CTCF motif; FOXA1 motif should rank high for 22Rv1 NIPBL.

E6.why: Label shuffling and dinucleotide-shuffled sequences are straightforward.

E7.why: A549 NIPBL peaks (11,343) are a second cell line; only 19% overlap with 22Rv1.

E8.why: No published ML number exists to reproduce; full text unavailable.

G2.why: ENCODE cohesin/TF ChIP-seq and AlphaGenome predictions, joinable on coordinates after liftover.

G3.why: Interval overlaps are manageable but need a liftover and overlap rule.

G4.why: Combining with ENCODE could test whether FOXA1-like pioneer factors explain NIPBL loading across cell types.

H1.why: Negatives are unbound background windows, constructed rather than measured.

H2.why: Two human cell lines with peak files; mouse tissues only as large bigWigs.

H3.why: Claim stated precisely below, limited to two cancer cell lines and single replicates.

H4.why: Missing peak files for mouse/LNCaP are visible in GEO; replicate limits not obvious.

I1.why: 3D-genome and cohesin community; prostate-cancer FOXA1 groups.

I2.why: Could prioritise cell types or loci for NIPBL ChIP, marginal impact.

I3.why: PR-AUC on held-out chromosomes roughly matches a ranking-of-sites use.

I4.why: A motif scan may do nearly as well; that must be tested first.

J1.why: Real modelling: chromosome splits, frozen DNA embeddings, cross-cell transfer.

J2.why: Motif enrichment gives some sanity checks; no domain expert lined up.

J3.why: Motif-baseline cross-cell analysis is shareable before any deep model.

J4.why: Roughly two weeks implied, not formally set.

J5.why: Kill condition written below; not yet in NOTES.md.

existing_models.name: FOXA1 sequence CNN (Molecular Cell 2024, PMC10659273)
existing_models.score_and_split: auPRC (area under the precision-recall curve) 0.20 vs 0.01 random for FOXA1 binding across 13 cell lines/tissues; split not checked.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not retrieved; models FOXA1 itself, not NIPBL.

existing_models.name: C.Origami (Nature Biotechnology 2023)
existing_models.score_and_split: Predicts cell-type-specific Hi-C contact maps from sequence + CTCF + accessibility; reported to beat Akita, DeepC, Orca. Split not checked.

existing_models.name: AkitaV2 (PLOS Computational Biology)
existing_models.score_and_split: Sequence-to-contact-map model used to interpret CTCF grammar; numbers not retrieved.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Only a minority of CTCF sites individually affect folding (from search snippet).

existing_models.name: Cohesin/RNA Pol II interaction CNN (NAR 2026, gkag258)
existing_models.score_and_split: Predicts cohesin-associated chromatin interactions; numbers not retrieved.

backbone.name: DNABERT-2 (DNA language model); alternative AlphaGenome via alphagenome-ft
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU, ~1-3 h to embed ~50k 1-kb windows (estimate)

integration.partner_dataset: ENCODE cohesin (RAD21/SMC3) and transcription-factor ChIP-seq across many cell lines
integration.join_key: Genomic coordinates (hg19, liftover to GRCh38 needed)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do the pioneer-factor motifs that predict NIPBL loading in prostate and lung cells also explain where cohesin enters chromatin in other cell types?

controls.positive_control: CTCF motif should predict RAD21 peaks; FOXA1 forkhead motif should be top feature for 22Rv1 NIPBL peaks (paper's main claim).
controls.negative_control: Shuffle labels; dinucleotide-shuffled sequences; per-chromosome shuffling.
controls.external_validation: A549 NIPBL peaks (11,343, 19% overlap with 22Rv1) as a second cell line; ENCODE cohesin peaks.

honest_claim_h3: Predicts whether a 500-bp hg19 window is a NIPBL ChIP-seq peak in one prostate-cancer (22Rv1) or one lung-cancer (A549) cell line, from single-replicate peak calls with randomly sampled unbound windows as negatives.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use DNA sequence to predict where the cohesin-loading protein lands in a given cell type, and test if it transfers between cell types.
plain_idea.train_on: 500-1,000-letter DNA windows from the human genome; 26,575 bound sites in prostate-cancer cells and 11,343 in lung-cancer cells (counted), plus sampled unbound windows.
plain_idea.predict: Whether the window is bound by NIPBL, measured by ChIP-seq (pulling down the protein and sequencing attached DNA) and called as peaks by MACS2.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Tells 3D-genome researchers whether cohesin entry sites are written in DNA plus cell-type factors, or need measuring in every new cell type.

more_or_better_data.why: NIPBL ChIP-seq in prostate and lung lines with FOXA1 perturbations is rare, but it is ~38k peaks from two cell lines, single replicates; generic models train on thousands of ENCODE tracks.

confidence_score.why: NIPBL tracks have one replicate each, so no replicate noise estimate is possible.

models_beatable.why: No NIPBL-specific model was found, so a motif baseline is the real competitor; generic sequence models (C.Origami 2023, AkitaV2) target contact maps, not loader binding.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No existing NIPBL model to run as baseline, so the 'same model plus new data on same split' condition fails.

label_elsewhere.sources: ENCODE hosts cohesin (RAD21/SMC3) ChIP-seq in many cell lines (known resource); NIPBL ChIP-seq exists in only a few public datasets (not searched systematically).
label_elsewhere.why: Cohesin peaks elsewhere would let a model trained here be tested on other cell types, though NIPBL itself is sparsely measured.

risks: Neighbouring or overlapping windows from the same peak landing in both train and test.
Background negatives with different GC content or mappability than peaks, letting the model learn GC rather than binding.
Repeat elements or segmental duplications that are near-identical across chromosomes.
Sequencing depth differences between conditions changing peak counts (1,349 vs 18,533) and masquerading as biology.
leakage_plan.split: Hold out whole chromosomes (e.g. chr8 and chr9 test, chr10 validation) using the narrowPeak chromosome column, seen in files; for transfer, train on 22Rv1 and test on A549.
checks: Shuffle labels and confirm PR-AUC drops to the positive fraction.
GC-matched negatives, and a GC-only model as a leaky-feature check.
Mask repeats and check test-train sequence similarity with a k-mer nearest-neighbour search.
leakage_plan.verdict: Manageable: chromosome hold-out and GC-matched negatives are standard, but depth confounds between conditions need care.

success_criteria.metric: PR-AUC on held-out chromosomes in A549 for a model trained on 22Rv1, because the use is ranking candidate loading sites in an unmeasured cell type.
success_criteria.baselines: Positive fraction (set by negative sampling); GC-content logistic regression; FOXA1 + ETS + CTCF motif-count logistic regression. No published number exists.
success_criteria.success: Frozen-embedding model beats the motif-count baseline by at least 0.10 PR-AUC on held-out chromosomes, both within 22Rv1 and transferred to A549 (thresholds set here, not from data).
success_criteria.kill: If after one week the embedding model is under 0.03 PR-AUC better than the motif baseline on held-out chromosomes, stop and write up the motif result.

ambitious.why: Publishes sequence-determinant studies of 3D genome; would need a clear, transferable sequence code for NIPBL loading validated on ENCODE cell types.

realistic.why: Takes modest computational re-analyses of public ChIP-seq; a cross-cell-line motif-versus-embedding comparison fits.

fallback.why: A negative result (motifs explain as much as deep embeddings) is still a useful short note.

pitch.headline: Public NIPBL binding maps in two human cancer lines share only 19% of sites, a cell-type specificity no sequence model has targeted.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: NIPBL ChIP-seq with FOXA1 degradation (26,575 vs 26,551 peaks, 65% retained) and FOXA1/ETS1 knockdowns in A549, all hg19 narrowPeak files under 1 MB. Mouse tissue tracks exist only as 263-505 MB bigWigs.
pitch.the_win: A sequence model trained on 22Rv1 that ranks A549 NIPBL sites at least 0.10 PR-AUC (precision-recall area) above a FOXA1/ETS motif scan on held-out chromosomes.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: Learn whether a simple motif scan already captures NIPBL placement, which tests the paper's pioneer-factor claim with an independent method.
pitch.who_wants_it: 3D-genome and cohesin labs, and prostate-cancer FOXA1 groups deciding whether NIPBL loading sites must be mapped experimentally in each new cell type.

ml_idea: Binary classifier of NIPBL-bound 500-bp windows from DNA sequence (frozen DNABERT-2 embeddings plus logistic head, against GC and FOXA1/ETS/CTCF motif-count baselines), evaluated on held-out chromosomes and transferred from 22Rv1 prostate to A549 lung cells.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: ~75k windows (positives plus matched negatives) at ~10 windows/s for DNABERT-2 on CPU; logistic head CV is minutes.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Fit a FOXA1+ETS+CTCF motif-count logistic regression on 22Rv1 NIPBL peaks vs GC-matched background; if held-out-chromosome PR-AUC is already near ceiling, there is no room for a deep model.

verdict_reason: Data is public and clean but small in scope: NIPBL peak files exist for only two human cell lines, single replicates, negatives must be sampled, and mouse tissue data are only large bigWigs. Sequence-to-binding is a standard task where a motif scan may suffice; worth doing only as a short transfer study.
